description.narrative:
Projektet GROW är ett strategiskt och väl genomtänkt initiativ för att stärka Kosovos privata sektor genom att ta itu med ihållande strukturella utmaningar, inklusive låg produktivitet, begränsad innovation, svag exportkapacitet och undermåliga företagsstödtjänster. I det tidigare projektet introducerades två initiativ, innovations- respektive exportfonden. Genom att skala upp dessa två till hållbara mekanismer förbättrar projektet effektivt viktiga marknadsfunktioner som produktdesign, digitalisering, kvalitetsstandarder, automatisering, turismhantering och exportfrämjande, och främjar på så sätt en mer konkurrenskraftig, inkluderande och motståndskraftig affärsmiljö.
GROW är väl anpassat till Sidas strategi för västra Balkan och Turkiet 2022–2027, Reformagendan och Sidas utvecklingsprioriteringar, som främjar inkluderande tillväxt, jämställdhetsanpassad utveckling, digital omvandling samt grön omställning genom energieffektivitet, cirkulär ekonomi, hållbar turism och ekodesign. Insatsens mål är ambitiösa, men bedöms kunna uppnås. Fram till 2029 ska GROW ha: gett stöd till 600 företag, skapat eller förbättrat 1 000 jobb, ökat omsättning med 12 miljoner, bidragit till 4 miljoner euro i nytillkommen export samt bidragit till 6 miljoner euro i offentliga och privata saminvesteringar genom hävstångseffekt.
Projektet stärker tjänsteleverantörer, kommuner, näringslivsorganisationer och viktiga institutioner som Kosovo Investment and Enterprise Support Agency (KIESA), snarare än att ersätta marknadsfunktioner vilket bidrar till bättre hållbarhet och ägarskap. GROW förutser proaktivt potentiella risker, inklusive begränsad servicekapacitet, långsam institutionell upptagning, exportvolatilitet och ojämlikt deltagande mellan män och kvinnor. Riskerna hanteras genom riktad utbildning, institutionell integrering, flexibla samfinansieringsmekanismer, marknadsdiversifierade insatser och verksamhet fokuserad på jämställdhet för att säkerställa inkluderande och varaktig effekt.

The GROW intervention represents a strategic and well-conceived initiative to strengthen Kosovo’s private sector by addressing persistent structural challenges, including low productivity, limited innovation, weak export capacity, and fragmented business-support services. By scaling up the Innovation Fund and Export Fund into sustainable mechanisms, the project effectively enhances key market functions such as product design, digitalization, quality standards, automation, tourism management, and export promotion, thereby fostering a more competitive, inclusive, and resilient business environment.
The intervention is well-aligned with Sida’s Strategy for the Western Balkans and Turkey 2022–2027, the Swedish Reform Agenda, and Sida’s development priorities, promoting inclusive growth, gender-responsive development, digital transformation, and the green transition through energy efficiency, circular practices, sustainable tourism, and eco-design. Its objectives are ambitious yet achievable, with projections indicating support for 600 enterprises, the creation or improvement of at least 1,000 jobs, €12 million in additional turnover, €4 million in new exports, and €6 million in leveraged public and private co-investments by 2029.
The intervention appropriately embeds sustainability by strengthening service providers, municipalities, business associations, and key institutions such as the Kosovo Investment and Enterprise Support Agency (KIESA), rather than substituting for market functions. It proactively anticipates potential risks, including limited service capacity, slow institutional uptake, export volatility, and uneven women’s participation and addresses them through targeted training, institutional embedding, flexible co-financing mechanisms, market diversification efforts, and focused gender outreach to ensure inclusive and durable impact.

The overall objective of GROW is to contribute to sustainable growth and increase access to productive economic opportunities for both individuals and enterprises within a growing private sector. This will be achieved by fostering a competitive, inclusive, and resilient market system in the targeted sectors, ultimately aiding Kosovos economic development through a more inclusive and competitive private-sector growth model. Building on the insights from the Fostering Employment and Growth Opportunities project, GROW will transition from direct enterprise-level support towards systemic market facilitation.
The focus will be on replicating, scaling, and adapting successful business models and services that drive enterprise growth, innovation, and competitiveness. GROW implements interventions that empower both enterprises and individuals to capitalize on emerging opportunities in Kosovos key sectors, helping them overcome critical constraints related to market offer, innovation, digitalization, and market access. GROW will pursue its goal through two interconnected outcomes that drive private-sector transformation:
Through Outcome 1 - Enterprises have strengthened competitiveness and improved their market offer
This outcome focuses on deepening firm level capacities, fostering innovation, diversifying products and offer, and embedding sustainable business practices. It aims to scale up pilot models from Fostering Employment and Growth Opportunities project through systemic, market-based approaches that engage sector associations, institutions, service providers, and academia in manufacturing sectors. Whereas, in rural tourism, the project aims to capitalize on its successful partnerships with local governments and the private sector to develop further and consolidate rural tourism offers in Kosovo. In doing so, the focus will be on institutionalizing sustainable operational and management systems for tourism destinations and on improving supporting services essential to fostering innovation and promoting quality standards in the sector.
This outcome focuses on the apparel, furniture, and rural tourism sectors, while also expanding into related value chains, including wood processing, prefabricated construction, and home and technical textiles. This approach leverages established networks and expertise to open new opportunities for innovation, diversification, and export growth.
Through Outcome 2 - Market actors have expanded trade access, promotion, and linkages
This outcome focuses on strengthening Kosovos international market presence and export linkages. It aims to build on the successful trade promotion and export models from Fostering Employment and Growth Opportunities project by developing sustainable, market-driven mechanisms for international promotion, destination branding, and B2B facilitation. Through collaboration with sector associations, export support institutions such as KIESA, and service providers, GROW will enable enterprises to improve their export readiness and investment promotion, participate more effectively in international fairs and B2B events, and access new buyers and distribution channels. In the rural tourism sector, the focus will be on enhancing destination branding and promotion and expanding the tourism offer to strategic marketing platforms.
While centered on the furniture, apparel, and rural tourism sectors, this outcome will also generate spill-over benefits across other manufacturing industries. As it focuses on developing trade-related services and promotion mechanisms, enterprises from additional sectors with emerging export potential, such as plastics, metal processing, or other niche industries, will be able to access and benefit from these market opportunities. This inclusive approach ensures that GROWs trade facilitation efforts strengthen Kosovos overall export ecosystem and diversify the countrys international market reach.
While both outcomes prioritize product diversification, quality improvement, innovation, digitalization, and green practices, alongside support for market-based solutions that boost enterprise performance, competitiveness, and long-term sustainability, by the end of the project: Outcome One will strengthen enterprise competitiveness and enhance the local market offering by scaling firm-level improvements and expanding market-driven business support services, and Outcome Two will expand market access and trade services by developing promotion channels, fostering B2B linkages, enhancing export readiness, and advancing destination branding.
